pr_title: stm32 LPTIM clock with prescaler to adjust the TICKS_PER_SEC
pr_body:
When the LPTIM is enabled for the lowPower (PM) purpose, the SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC is set to a lower value (than default 10000)

- 4000 if LPTIM is clocked by LSI (32000Hz)
- 4096 if LPTIM is clocked by LSE (32768Hz)

However when the lptim has a <prescaler> that divides the clock source , this SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC is even too high, resulting in numerous system wakeup during sleep mode (no more sleeping indeed)
Consequently the SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC is set to a value depending 
 on the clock input LSE/LSI and the clock prescaler property set in the DTS
- 1000 if LPTIM is clocked by LSI (32000Hz)  divided by 32 
- 1024 if LPTIM is clocked by LSE (32768Hz)  divided by 32 
- 2000 if LPTIM is clocked by LSI (32000Hz)  divided by 16 
- 2048 if LPTIM is clocked by LSE (32768Hz)  divided by 16

Removing SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC in the board config and adding
Warning build message to check the coherency between
- clock source definition (LSI/LSE) and the board DTS (lptim node <clocks> property)
- SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC and the LPTIM clock ratio (lptim node <st,prescaler> property) 

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/61099

@FRASTM Do you think we can replace the whole prescaler/frequency Kconfig based check by a runtime version ?
I expect a runtime check to be much more simple. Drawback is that misconfiguration would be discovered later, but it doesn't prevent to provide a clear message to the user.

Also, we should add a comment in `dts/bindings/timer/st,stm32-lptim.yaml` on the new constraint.

Last, in the PR, addition of `stm32_lp_tick_source` in boards description should be done before adding the code that uses it, in order to avoid failures (on a git bisect for instance).

> @FRASTM Do you think we can replace the whole prescaler/frequency Kconfig based check by a runtime version ? I expect a runtime check to be much more simple. Drawback is that misconfiguration would be discovered later, but it doesn't prevent to provide a clear message to the user.


The warning message will still check CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC and the ratio CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_CLOCK/LPTIM_PRESCALER, whatever the CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_CLOCK is LSE or LSI.
However  this warning message  can be put a common macro : 
```
#if ((CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC > CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_CLOCK/LPTIM_PRESCALER) && \
	(LPTIM_PRESCALER >= 16))
#warning ...
```

issue_context.title: Sample STM32PM Blinky higher energy usage on nucleo_wb55rg since adding prescaler for lptim1
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
When running the sample stm32 power_mgmt blinky (zephyr/samples/boards/stm32/power_mgmt/blinky/) on the nucleo_wb55rg board, the microcontroller seems to wake up from sleep every 2 ms. This causes higher energy-usage than expected (on average between 600 and 700 uA when the LED is off).
With an older version of zephyr (before commit 29ef82cfaf02a6171eb85462bda73d11e7bd84bf), the microcontroller did not wake up so frequently, and the current was a about 100 to 130 uA with the LED off. 

My assumption is that is has to do with the prescaler which is set to 32 in the overlay for the nucleo_wb55rg. This results in 1024 ticks per second, but the default CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC is at 4096.
When I set the prescaler to 8 in nucleo_wb55rg.overlay, or the CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC to 1024 in prj.conf, the microcontroller does not wake up that often, and the energy-usage is about the same as before commit 29ef82cfaf02a6171eb85462bda73d11e7bd84bf. Each of these changes (changing prescaler, or changing  CONFIG_SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC) can solve the problem, but I don't know the root cause of the problem, and do not know if this is the desired solution.


**To Reproduce**
build the example:
west build -b nucleo_wb55rg samples/boards/stm32/power_mgmt/blinky

flash it to the microcontroller
west flash

Analyse the energy-consumption

**Expected behavior**
I expect the microcontroller to be sleeping for longer periods of time than 2 ms

**Impact**
Higher enenergy-consumption than expected

**Logs and console output**
Current with sample:
![afbeelding](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/141256366/44768713-e1b6-4306-8c2c-dfca12b40559)



Detail of current with peak every 2 ms:
![afbeelding](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/141256366/196a7389-0dac-4385-a43b-15211fceef1d)



Current with prescaler at 8:
![afbeelding](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/assets/141256366/064f4b91-774e-490d-93c7-36acac52a0af)



**Environment:**
 - OS: Linux
 - Toolchain: zephyr-sdk-0.16.1
 - Commit SHA or Version used: 0a2d538c2bc442e64b3b86f3cf05a311223466ac

**Additional context**
When the current is measured in the nucleo wb55rg, the jumpers for the STlink (JP5) are removed, the USB-cable disconnected, and voltage supplied via JP2.

review_comments: This could be removed following previous comment.

Since the Kconfig is deprecated, I think it would be better to use `#if (DT_INST_CLOCKS_CELL_BY_IDX(0, 1, bus) != STM32_SRC_LSI)` instead and remove all previous uses of `CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_CLOCK_LSI`. It's been deprecated for some time now.
Same with the `#elif (CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_CLOCK_LSE)`.

I understand your comment, but I propose to have another PR for this change :  get the LPTIM clock source index from clock source selected in the DTS of the stm32_lp_tick_source node.
This is done with 
` #define CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_CLOCK DT_INST_CLOCKS_CELL_BY_IDX(0, 1, bus)`
and comparing `CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_CLOCK == STM32_SRC_LSI ` or `CONFIG_STM32_LPTIM_CLOCK == STM32_SRC_LSE`

When STM32_SRC_LSE and STM32_SRC_LSI have always the same value among all the stm32 series.

It seems, at first approach, there will be a problem reading the device Tree property  `$(dt_inst_clocks_cell_by_idx(0, 1, bus))` directly in the Kconfig  (no macro available) since it is needed to set the config SYS_CLOCK_TICKS_PER_SEC
